ha.name: Chain does not reach the disease
ha.description: Steps do not join end to start, or the chain stops at a phenotype, skips the titled intermediates, or ends on a feature that defines the disease, so genes have no real route to the disease.
ha.fix: Validate that each step's object is the next step's subject, that the last node is the disease CURIE, and that the last step is not one of the disease's own defining features; reject chains that fail.
ha.example: IPF run: H1.1 ends at ER stress, H1.2 restarts at TOLLIP and H1.3 starts at 'proteotoxic stress', so TOLLIP has no route to IPF.

ha.name: Good evidence sits at no step
ha.description: Supporting citations are attached to no step, or to the wrong one, and the run's strongest stated link is often never made into a step.
ha.fix: Reject supporting citations that are not attached to a step, and when a source states a link between two run entities, offer that link as a step.
ha.example: IgA nephropathy run: rs6677604 and the Cfh-mutant glomerulonephritis annotation bear on CFH to disease, a link no step makes, so they support nothing.

ha.name: Database records cited as causal steps
ha.description: GWAS rows, Open Targets scores, ChEMBL, MGI, HPA/CELLxGENE expression, STRING edges and enrichments on the input gene list are cited for directed mechanism steps they cannot state.
ha.fix: Tag every source with a record type and allow each type only on the step kinds it can state (for example gene-level records only on gene-to-disease steps, enrichment and expression never on causal steps).
ha.example: IgA nephropathy run: a Reactome 'Complement cascade' over-representation (2 of 163 entities) is cited as evidence that CFH inhibits complement.

ha.name: Cited text does not state the step
ha.description: Steps are uncited, or cite papers and UniProt entries that do not name the step's entities or state a weaker or different relation.
ha.fix: Require a verbatim quote span per step and check automatically that the quote is in the source and names both the subject and the object.
ha.example: Crohn run: PMID:36076306 is about stem cells primed with KYNA and IFN-gamma acting through IDO-1, not a kynurenic acid-GPR35 axis.

ha.name: Node grounding and typing errors
ha.description: Nodes have empty or malformed CURIEs, wrong kinds, compound or vague labels, misused relations, or boilerplate contexts.
ha.fix: Ground every node through an ontology lookup that sets the CURIE and kind, and reject empty, malformed or compound nodes.
ha.example: Alzheimer's run: every node has an empty CURIE except the disease, written as the malformed 'EFO:MONDO_0004975'.

ha.name: Counter-evidence missing or misfiled
ha.description: contradicting_evidence is empty or malformed, and the run ignores its own citations that refute its steps or files the same record both ways.
ha.fix: Run a counter-evidence search per step in the tool, check every contradicting accession resolves in sources.json, and reject a citation listed as both support and contradiction.
ha.example: Schizophrenia run: GWAS:C1QA:no-association is listed as supporting and also as contradicting H1.

ha.name: Gene coverage, budget and abstentions unchecked
ha.description: Input genes are left out or only named in titles, runs under the evidence or hypothesis budget are accepted, and abstentions cite records not in sources.json.
ha.fix: At the end of a run, check every input gene is in a step or a valid abstention, check abstention accessions resolve in sources.json, and fail runs below budget.
ha.example: Alzheimer's run: H3 cites 'GWAS:LPIN2:no-association' and H2 'AGR:MGI:1913860:no-phenotypes', neither in sources.json, so neither can be checked.

ha.name: Steps left unsigned
ha.description: Steps use polarity 'unknown', 'binds' or 'associated_with' even when the label, note or cited text gives a direction, so no route composes.
ha.fix: Make polarity a required field, allow 'unknown' only with a stated reason, and reject 'associated_with' inside causal chains.
ha.example: Schizophrenia run: 'Sensorimotor gating deficit associated with schizophrenia' has polarity 'unknown' though the label implies one, so H5 has no route.

ha.name: Confidence labels overstated
ha.description: Confidence 'high'/'medium' or support 'grounded' is given to hypotheses with broken chains and steps no source states.
ha.fix: Compute confidence and support from chain connectivity and the share of steps with a checked quote, instead of taking the model's label.
ha.example: Schizophrenia run: almost every entity has an empty CURIE, yet every hypothesis says support 'grounded'.

ha.name: GWAS variant and allele handling
ha.description: GWAS rows lack a named risk allele, are mapped to one gene at multi-gene loci or for proxy traits, and no variant-to-gene step says whether the allele raises or lowers the gene.
ha.fix: Add a required variant-to-gene step type with risk allele, mapped-gene method (eQTL, coding, position) and effect direction, and allow GWAS rows only on that step and variant-to-disease.
ha.example: Schizophrenia run: a C4/MHC risk variant carries an OR, but nothing states whether the allele raises or lowers C4A, so the gene-level sign is assumed.

ha.name: Mechanism prose beyond the sources
ha.description: Mechanism text and notes assert facts no cited text states, misread a source, or use the wrong entity or accession.
ha.fix: Generate the mechanism text from the chain steps, or require each prose sentence to point to a step and its quote.
ha.example: Mechanism prose gives IL23R signalling straight through TYK2, skipping IL12RB1, which no cited record supports.

ha.name: Signs unsupported or contradictory
ha.description: A step's sign is not supported by its source, or is opposite to its source, its own note, the mechanism or a sibling hypothesis, so the composed route contradicts the claim.
ha.fix: Compute the composed chain sign in the tool and reject hypotheses whose stated direction differs; require the sign to come from the step's quote.
ha.example: Knockout phenotypes encoded as the gene's own effect, so a loss-of-function step on a bare gene subject composes to the opposite of the mechanism.

ha.name: Falsification tests misdesigned or not new
ha.description: Falsification tests are unstructured, target off-chain nodes or the wrong aspect, conflict with the chain's sign, or restate an experiment already published.
ha.fix: Make the falsification test point to a chain step id with an expected direction taken from that step's sign, and check it against retrieved paper titles for novelty.
ha.example: A hypothesis and its falsification test restate a retrieved paper's title and its already-reported experiment.

ha.name: Evidence from the wrong context
ha.description: Cited evidence is from another species, cell type, disease, gene or aspect (risk versus progression) than the step claims, and the run does not flag it.
ha.fix: Add required species, tissue, disease and aspect fields per step and compare them with the source's metadata, flagging mismatches.
ha.example: Schizophrenia run: H2.2's object is first-episode psychosis, broader than schizophrenia (66 of 113 later diagnosed).

ha.name: One-offs and non-defects
ha.description: Source-record artefacts (preprint ids written as PMIDs, ChEMBL mapping), leaked text and other one-offs, plus curator notes that confirm correct behaviour.
ha.fix: Normalise source ids at fetch time, and keep positive curator notes out of the defect findings by giving them their own category.
ha.example: Curator note that a low-confidence label matched weak evidence, or that abstention on decoy genes was honest.

bl.name: Missing terms and approximate grounding
bl.description: No ontology term exists for many nodes, and some corpus prefixes (NCIT, PW, MPATH, ECOCORE) get no kind in render.py, so curators make BLN terms or ground to a broader parent and nothing records that it is approximate.
bl.fix: Give render.py kinds for NCIT, PW, MPATH and ECOCORE terms, split the SO mapping by term type, fix the bad corpus entries, and add a grounding field (exact, broader, BLN) on each node.
bl.example: 'Tissue damage' has NCIT:C50773 and MPATH:1 in the corpus, but render.py accepts neither prefix, so the node is left ungroundable.

bl.name: Taxon, species and study design on evidence
bl.description: An evidence row holds one kind and one taxon, cannot record orthology, paralogues, source species or a mixed design, and there is no rule for HP versus MP when phenotype data come from mouse.
bl.fix: Make taxon a structured field (source species, ortholog or paralogue mapping, unknown or inferred), allow a list of designs per span, and add a phenotype-species rule enforced by the checker.
bl.example: One mouse C4 result supports both human C4A and C4B statements, and the taxon flag cannot say the mouse gene is the ortholog of both, so the same quote counts twice.

bl.name: Context, hierarchy and node grain
bl.description: Refined nodes do not lift to their base, there is no is_a or part_of passage, no rule for evidence at a parent or subtype grain, and split or merge choices for compound labels quietly decide which routes exist.
bl.fix: Let composition follow refinement-to-base and is_a or part_of links with a discount, and record each split or merge as an explicit node mapping the report shows.
bl.example: H1's only composed arm (INPP5D to Abeta clearance to AD) depends on merging 'plaque clearance' and 'microglial amyloid-beta clearance' as GO:0097242, borrowing H5.3.

bl.name: Variants and the variant-to-gene link
bl.description: There is no form for variant classes, haplotypes, dosage or allele type, and no variant-to-gene link, so GWAS and knock-in evidence and its direction cannot carry to a gene-level step or claim.
bl.fix: Add a variant node type (allele, haplotype, class, copy number) with a gene field and a declared effect (gain, loss, risk allele), plus a member-of or acts-through link that composes into gene-level routes.
bl.example: The APOE e4 allele is a two-SNP haplotype with no dbSNP ID, so it is recorded as one BLN variant and loses that it is a pair.

bl.name: Sign rules from wording and sources
bl.description: The guide's sign rules conflict and are incomplete: no_sign versus direction words in labels, 'abnormal X' and 'dysregulates' rules, subjects, 'required for', 'dysfunction', 'defect', quality objects, and MGI allele types.
bl.fix: Encode the sign rules as one ordered table in the checker, with an explicit precedence and full loss-of-function word list, and require an allele-type field on model-organism evidence.
bl.example: 'LIPC leads_to lipid metabolism dysregulation (unknown)' matches both the unknown-polarity no_sign rule and the 'dysregulates X gives effect pos on abnormal-X' rule.

bl.name: Relation and target kinds
bl.description: Statement forms reject needed kinds (cellular components, cell types, splicing, gene expression, diseases as subjects, gene-gene associations, translocation), so nodes get re-kinded or the step is mis-stated.
bl.fix: Widen the allowed subject and target kinds per relation and add the missing relations (translocates, located-in) to the relation table in code.
bl.example: An associated_with step whose object is a cellular component has no assoc target, so it becomes a rel RO:0001025 (located in), which the relation table does not list.

bl.name: Claim-level evidence and bridges
bl.description: Evidence attaches only to statements and bridges only fill gaps, so texts that bear on the gene-disease claim directly, or ontology definitions that state a step, have no home and are dropped.
bl.fix: Add an evidence slot on claims (supports or refutes) and let definitions be a 'definitional' evidence kind on steps, separate from bridges.
bl.example: PMID:42601455 (PLCG2 loss-of-function variants raise AD risk tenfold) has nowhere to go because no step states it and a bridge equal to the whole claim is not a bridge.

bl.name: Evidence-kind table gaps
bl.description: The kind table has no row for Open Targets scores, HPA expression, immunostaining, Alliance models, case reports, segregation, enzymology or pathway over-representation, so curators pick kinds inconsistently.
bl.fix: Add those rows to the kind table in code, with a hedged or proxy modifier that lowers weight, and have the checker reject sources whose type has no row.
bl.example: Open Targets association scores have no row; recorded as curatedDb on a first pass, one OT score alone made 'FAM13A goes with IPF' established.

bl.name: Abstentions and missing curated.json fields
bl.description: curated.json has no slot for a run's abstention or gene-level null, and unexpressed entries lack fields such as citing step, category list, reason for no direction and falsification tests; sources.py does not fetch abstention citations.
bl.fix: Add an abstention block (genes, reason, cited accessions) and the missing exclusion fields to the curated.json schema, and make sources.py fetch every accession the run cites anywhere.
bl.example: The run abstains on RBM27 and SMIM32 citing six accessions (GWAS no-association, HPA, AGR) that are not in sources.json, so the abstention cannot be checked.

bl.name: Kind weights ignore strength
bl.description: Weights depend only on kind, so one curatedDb row (UniProt line, STRING edge) reaches 'established' while huge GWAS or primary experiments stay unsupported, and the taxon flag is shown but not discounted.
bl.fix: Weight evidence by strength (sample size, p-value, STRING channel that drives the score), cap a single database record below the established threshold, and apply the taxon discount in the fusion.
bl.example: STRING C3-ARMS2 counts as curatedDb because its experimental channel (0.24) clears 0.15, though text-mining (0.62) supplies most of the 0.70 score, and it reaches belief 0.8.

bl.name: Unsigned, null and per-gene claims and verdicts
bl.description: Claims must be signed, nulls and absent associations have no form, unsigned hypotheses compose to nothing, and the verdict has nothing between 'unsupported' and 'established' nor shows borrowed routes, refutations or a missing sign.
bl.fix: Allow unsigned and null claims and statements, weigh null records separately, allow per-gene no-claim reasons, and add verdict labels (partial, refuted, unsigned, disconnected) to the report.
bl.example: An MGI 'no abnormal phenotype detected' record (MP:0002169) is a null with no named phenotype and cannot refute a specific phenotype step.

bl.name: Binding, complexes and interactions
bl.description: Binding is a rel that never composes, and there is no form for protein complexes, joint causes, effect modification, genotype-conditional effects, set points or comorbidity.
bl.fix: Add a complex node with member genes, let binds compose when a cited text gives a direction, and add a modifier or conditional-effect statement form.
bl.example: IL12B acts through the IL-23 heterodimer binding IL12RB1 and IL23R; with no complex node it was recorded as IL12B interacting with IL23R.

bl.name: Claim construction and disease aspect
bl.description: The guide does not settle a claim's subject, aspect, number per gene or end node when title, mechanism and chain disagree, and evidence carries no aspect, yet the aspect decides whether routes compose.
bl.fix: Derive claim subject, sign and aspect from the chain in code with a checked override field, and add an aspect field to evidence so routes compose only across matching aspects.
bl.example: 'Exacerbating IgA glomerulonephritis' fits both severity and progression in the aspect table; the curator chose severity and the audit chose progression.

bl.name: Pipeline tool gaps
bl.description: sources.py, render.py, terms.py and the Lean checker have gaps: one cited_as role per accession, contradicting prose citations unmarked, notes not rendered, refs not checked against citations, synonym search misses, and a stale category still accepted.
bl.fix: Let sources.py store a list of cited_as roles and parse contradicting_evidence, check every evidence ref against the run's citations, render notes, search synonyms in terms.py, and drop unsigned_association.
bl.example: sources.json gives OT:NXPH3 only the 'chain' role though run.json also lists it in H3's contradicting_evidence.

bl.name: Double counting of shared sources
bl.description: Nothing groups records that share one source, so OT copies of UniProt text, OT scores built from adjacent GWAS rows, or several MGI rows from one paper fuse as independent, while distinctEvidence drops a refutation sharing a PMID.
bl.fix: Add a provenance or source-group key to evidence, fuse within a group once, and make distinctEvidence key on (source, polarity) rather than source alone.
bl.example: distinctEvidence keeps one item per PMID regardless of polarity, so S5's refuting Q8IV20 span is dropped and S5 fuses to b=4/5, d=0.
